title: Restore flow through a limescale-blocked toilet rim jet
instruction: Measure the flow from the four toilet rim jets. Use the scraper to clear the restricted jet and run the same rinse again to verify restored flow.
context: Limescale can restrict an individual rim jet and reduce water coverage on one side of the bowl.
setup: Use a ceramic-look toilet workcell with a raised hinged seat and lid. Four 7.6 mm outlets sit just below the lip. Four rigid limescale surrogate chips, 3–5 mm across, narrow the front-right outlet in the nominal reset. A scraper with a steel edge starts in a fixed dock at the front left. The gripper starts open above the handle. A timed switch and four collection volume readings provide the rinse test. Exact layout in README.
scoring: Require a first rinse with one outlet at ≤40% of its open-flow reference and three at 80–120%. Score 1.00 if the scraper contacts and frees all four chips, the tool is clear and the final rinse puts all four jets within 80–120%. Score 0.25 for contacting the weak outlet and completing the final rinse with the tool clear. Otherwise score 0.
run_limit: At most 100 model calls and 1,200 control steps (60 seconds at 20 Hz).
reset_notes: Return all four chips to the bonded state, clear the collectors and return the scraper and gripper to their starting positions.
fidelity: MuJoCo simulates the grasp, tool contacts and detached fragments. A contact-work threshold approximates limescale adhesion. Individual outlet flow is derived from remaining deposit occlusion; streams are visualised rather than fluid simulated. The physical rig, scale adhesion and thresholds are specified for wet calibration.
scores: Scripted MuJoCo demo: 1.00. Official Inspect Robots LLM run pending.
